waveName: Wave 2 – Workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours & preview, photo intake, design system

package.title: Grout-aware honest preview and grout colour recommendation
package.goal: The zoomed-out view, the PDF preview and thumbnails show what the wall will look like from a distance, including grout. Laid stones stay visible at any zoom. The joint step recommends the grout colour that gives the best effect from a distance and shows that estimated deviation.
steps:
buildOverviewRGBA(layout, data, palette, groutHex):
- Footprint per cell: fw = colW + g/2 on each inner side, same for fh.
- Covered area: colW·rowH for FULL cells, Σ area(cellPieces) otherwise.
- Mix: (Σ a·lin(c) + rest·lin(grout)) / max(A, covered), in linear light, using 256- and 4096-entry LUTs.
- Fix the doc comment.
- renderFull passes opt.groutHex ?? '#BDB8AE'. Viewer passes props.groutHex and adds it to the memo dependencies.

Overview path (pitch < 3 px): draw a second 1 px-per-cell overlay for progressMode (laid cells) and for focusColor dimming. In the detailed path, show laid stones with a desaturating grey-green tint instead of a white wash, and show the check mark from 6 px.
Viewer: read --viewer-bg once on mount and on theme change, not on every draw.

grout.ts:
- GROUT_CANDIDATES with generic names (Weiß #F2F0EA, Hellgrau/Beige #BDB8AE, Silbergrau #9A9A96, Zementgrau #808080, Dunkelgrau #5A5A5A, Anthrazit #404040, Schwarz #202020), plus the current colour.
- cellCoverage(layout, data?), computed per cell from the actual piece areas.
- perceivedDeltaE(targetLinPerCell, stoneLinPerCell|null, coverage, groutLin, sigmaCells=2): Gaussian blur over the cell grid in linear light, then mean and p95 ΔE00 against the blurred photo.
- recommendGrout(...): ranked results.

StepGeometry joint step:
- Compute the recommendation on the cropped photo downsampled to at most about 200k cells (reuse renderCropped read-only).
- Show 'Empfehlung: Dunkelgrau – Fernwirkung ΔE ≈ x (aktuell y) – Schätzung' with an 'Übernehmen' button. Never change the user's grout colour automatically.
- When a mosaic has been computed, also show 'Fernwirkung inkl. Fuge (Modell-Schätzung)' for the current grout, based on the computed stone colours.
- Add the hint that grout dries lighter, so the user should enter the HEX of a dried sample.
acceptance: recommendGrout on the portrait sample at default settings ranks a darker grout than #BDB8AE, with lower perceived ΔE. It does not force a dark grout on the animal sample.

e2e phone 390×844 with the landscape sample: zooming one step across the overview threshold changes the mean colour of the centre crop by ΔE76 < 3 (today 11.3). Changing the grout colour changes the overview pixels.
e2e lay mode at fit zoom: laid stones are visible in the overview.
package.risk: Effort M. This only changes display and estimates; geometry and counts are untouched. The PDF picks up the new overview automatically through renderFull.

findings.title: Grout colour dominates how the finished mosaic looks, but colour matching ignores it (the default light grout washes out every photo)
findings.problem: computeMosaic matches each stone to the photo as if stones covered 100 % of the surface. With 5 mm stones and a 1 mm joint the grout covers 30.6 % of the area (8 mm/1 mm: 21 %). From a normal viewing distance the eye mixes stones and grout in linear light, so the default grout #BDB8AE (src/core/types.ts:212) lifts every dark area (suit, hair, pupils) and desaturates skin. The diagnostics shown on the compute step (StepCompute.tsx:90-94, fed by track() in mosaic.ts) compare only the stone colour with the cell mean. They report 'ΔE ≈ 1.6–3.5', which hides the problem.
findings.evidence: Script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/algo-quality/exp-grout.ts, output in .../algo-quality/out/results/exp-grout.txt. Perceived ΔE00 = Gaussian blur over the full render including grout, σ = 2 pitches, linear light, compared with the blurred photo. Default grout #BDB8AE: obama 40 cm/5 mm 12.8 mean / 29.4 p95; astronaut 10.8/30.0; coffee 12.7/24.8; synthetic portrait sample 11.5/23.9. Same stones with grout #404040: 6.0/8.5, 6.7/9.1, 6.1/7.9, 5.7/8.1. Prototype .../algo-quality/exp-grout-comp.ts (output .../out/results/exp-grout-comp.txt): stone target t' = (t − (1−f)·g)/f in linear RGB, then k-means and matching. Dark grout plus full compensation reaches 2.0/5.1 (obama), 2.7/7.2 (astronaut), 2.3/5.6 (coffee). With the light default grout, compensation cannot help (11.5/28.8) because the darks are out of reach. Visual: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/algo-quality/out/grout-distance-view.png (source | app default | dark grout | dark grout + compensation, downscaled to simulate distance). Photos: public-domain NASA/US-gov portraits and CC0 skimage samples in .../algo-quality/dl/photos/.
findings.proposal: (1) S – Recommend a grout colour. Evaluate a short list of real grout colours (white, light grey, beige, mid grey, anthracite, black) on the downsampled working image in linear light, with stone coverage f = tileW·tileH/((tileW+g)(tileH+g)) from the layout. Preselect the colour with the lowest perceived ΔE and show that number in the joint step (StepGeometry). (2) M – Optional grout-aware colour targets in computeMosaic. Before k-means and matching, convert each cell/piece target to linear RGB and apply t' = clamp((t − (1−f_s)·g)/f_s), where f_s = 1 − s·(1−f) and s is a 'Fernwirkung' strength slider (0–100 %, default 50 %). Match by ΔE00(t', palette). The stone dialog keeps showing the original photo colour, so nothing is hidden. (3) S – Add an honest 'Fernwirkung ΔE' diagnostic (blur including grout) next to the existing ΔE. Expected: perceived mean ΔE about −50 % from the grout choice alone and about −80 % with compensation on real photos.
corrected:

- Compute it on the working image, downsampled to about one pixel per cell. For each candidate g, take the mean and p95 of ΔE00(f·t + (1−f)·g, t) in linear RGB, where t is the photo colour and f = tileW·tileH/((tileW+joint)(tileH+joint)).
- Show the best candidate with its ΔE next to the grout colour picker, plus a one-click 'Übernehmen' button.
- Never override the user's chosen or default grout on its own.
- Recompute when tile size, joint width or image changes.

2) (S) Honest distance preview.
- In buildOverviewRGBA (src/core/render.ts:93), blend each cell's colour with the grout colour in linear light, using that cell's coverage f_cell. Then the zoomed-out view (render.ts:165) shows the real effect instead of stone colours only.
- Optionally add a 'Fernwirkung' toggle in the Viewer that renders the whole mosaic this way at any zoom level.

3) (S) Distance diagnostic in StepCompute. Add a second row, 'Farbabweichung aus Entfernung inkl. Fuge (Schätzung)': mean and p95 ΔE00 of f_cell·stone + (1−f_cell)·grout against the photo cell, computed in linear light. f_cell = (sum of the cell's piece polygon areas from cellPieces/subRects) / ((colW+joint)·(rowH+joint)). Label it as an estimate and state its assumption: the joints blend into the stones at viewing distance.

4) (M, optional, default OFF) Grout-aware colour targets in computeMosaic.
- Add a 'Fugenkompensation' slider (0–100 %, default 0).

- Store s in the project settings and show it in the PDF and legend.
- The stone dialog keeps the original photo colour, the chosen stone colour and both ΔE values.
- Add tests: with s=0 the output is identical to today; with s>0 the distance ΔE drops on the sample images and nothing else changes (counts, geometry, cut dimensions).

(1) S/M, do this first: a grout recommendation instead of silently preselecting a colour.
- Add the function `recommendGrout(img, layout, candidates)` in a new src/core/grout.ts.
- Candidates are generic named colours, not brands: Weiß #F2F0EA, Hellgrau/Beige #BDB8AE, Silbergrau #9A9A96, Zementgrau #808080, Dunkelgrau #5A5A5A, Anthrazit #404040, Schwarz #202020, plus the user's current groutHex.
- Model it analytically on the cell grid, so no rasterisation is needed and it scales to millions of stones in 64-cell tiles. For each cell take the linear-RGB cell mean t. Before compute, use the photo; after compute, use the assigned stone colour. Perceived colour = f·t + (1−f)·g, with f = tileW·tileH/((tileW+joint)(tileH+joint)) from the layout. Apply a Gaussian blur over cells with σ = 2 cells, convert to Lab, and take ΔE00 against the blurred photo.
- In StepGeometry, next to the grout colour picker, show 'Empfehlung: Dunkelgrau – Fernwirkung ΔE ≈ 6 (aktuell 12,8)' with an 'Übernehmen' button. Never overwrite the user's choice or their Settings default automatically.
- Label it as an estimate. Add a note that real grout dries lighter and differs between brands, so the user should enter the HEX of a dried sample.
- Optionally, change the factory default (types.ts:212, db.ts:124) from #BDB8AE to #808080. That halves far-view ΔE in every case tested.

(2) S: honest diagnostics in StepCompute.
- Rename the existing value to 'ΔE Stein ↔ Foto (Nahansicht)'.
- Add 'Fernwirkung inkl. Fuge (Modell-Schätzung)', computed with the same cell-grid model in the worker after compute (mosaic.ts diagnostics, or a separate worker message).
- Recompute it when the grout changes without recomputing the mosaic, because only the grout term changes.

(3) M, optional and OFF by default: grout-aware colour targets.
- Add `groutCompensation` (0–100 %, default 0) and pass `groutLin` and `f` into ComputeParams.
- Before k-means sampling and before matching (mosaic.ts:417-541), map each cell/piece target t to t' = (t − (1−f_s)·g)/f_s in linear RGB, with f_s = 1 − s_eff·(1−f).
- Compute s_eff per stone and channel as min(s, t/(g(1−f)), (1−t)/((1−f)(1−g))), so targets never clip. Plain clamping crushed shadow detail in testing.
- Add groutHex and s to computeKey (useProject.ts:18) only when s > 0, so grout changes stay preview-only when compensation is off.
- Show a hint when the grout is lighter than the median image L*: 'Kompensation hilft bei heller Fuge kaum – dunklere Fuge wählen'.
- Add the original photo colour and its ΔE to StoneDialog. It is not shown there today.
- Tests:
  - stone and colour totals stay identical to the assignment counts;
  - with s = 0 the result is bit-identical to the current behaviour;
  - with dark grout and s = 50 %, far ΔE goes down and near ΔE stays at or below about 4.5 on the sample portrait.

findings.title: Zoomed-out preview, PDF preview and thumbnails show the mosaic without grout and blend cut cells 50/50
findings.problem: buildOverviewRGBA (render.ts:93-131) averages c1/c2 of split cells 50/50 regardless of their actual areas, in sRGB, and ignores the grout. renderMosaic draws this bitmap whenever the pitch is under 3 px or more than 400 k cells are visible (render.ts:165-168). renderFull uses it too, for the PDF preview at 2400 px (StepPdf.tsx:44) and for project thumbnails at 320 px (useProject.ts:329). On a phone, or for projects of roughly 1 m and larger, the whole-picture view therefore shows a darker, more saturated mosaic than the one that will actually be built. This undermines the 'realistic preview' requirement.
findings.evidence: Script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/algo-quality/exp-misc.ts (output .../out/results/exp-misc.txt, check 'overview-vs-optical-mix'), obama 40 cm/5 mm/1 mm. The overview colour differs from the true optical mix of each cell's pitch area (pieces + grout, linear light) by ΔE00 16.5 mean, 31.1 p95. For the 714 split cells alone, ignoring grout, the difference is 4.9 mean, 12.1 p95, 21.2 max.
findings.proposal: In buildOverviewRGBA compute, per cell, the coverage-weighted mean in linear RGB: Σ area(piece)·lin(colour) + (pitchArea − Σ area(piece))·lin(grout), divided by pitchArea, then convert back to sRGB. Piece areas come from the cellPieces polygons; cache them per CellKind/line signature. Pass groutHex in from Viewer, renderFull and the thumbnail code. The zoomed-out view, PDF preview and thumbnails then match how the mosaic will actually look, and use the same metric as the first finding.
corrected:
1. Change the signature to buildOverviewRGBA(layout, data, palette, groutHex) in src/core/render.ts. For each cell, compute the colour of the footprint that its overview pixel is stretched over: fw = finishedW/cols, fh = finishedH/rows, A = fw*fh.
   - FULL cells: stoneArea = colW[col]*rowH[row], with the colour of c1.
   - All other cells: take Σ area(poly) and colour from cellPieces(layout, data, row, col). Only about 5 % of cells are not FULL, so no cache is needed.
   - groutArea = max(0, A − stoneArea).
   - Pixel = (Σ a_i·lin(c_i) + groutArea·lin(grout)) / (stoneArea + groutArea), mixed in linear light (physically correct for viewing at a distance), then converted back to sRGB.
   This also fixes the 50/50 weighting of LINE cells, FREE pieces weighted by count, and the inner joints of SUB cells. Fix the doc comment at line 92 to match.
2. Viewer.tsx:44-53: pass props.groutHex to buildOverviewRGBA and add it to the useMemo dependency list, so the overview is rebuilt when the grout colour changes.
3. renderFull (render.ts:348): pass opt.groutHex ?? '#BDB8AE'. useProject.ts:329 and StepPdf.tsx:44 already pass groutHex to renderFull, so they need no changes.
4. Add a vitest test:
   - For a FULL cell with joint g, the pixel equals the analytic coverage mix.
   - For a LINE cell, the weights equal the polygon areas.
   - On a sample mosaic, the mean overview colour stays within a small ΔE of a fine rasterisation that includes grout.
5. Optional: compare pitchPx against devicePixelRatio·scale instead of CSS px. On phones with dpr 3 the full per-stone render could then be used down to about 1 CSS px, which reduces how often the overview is shown at all.
This shows no invented data. It only makes the preview at a distance consistent with the per-stone render and with the physical result.

Make the overview an exact optical mix of each cell: area-weighted, in linear light, with grout. The change is display-only.

1. Change the signature to buildOverviewRGBA(layout, data, palette, groutHex) in src/core/render.ts. Precompute:
   - a 256-entry lookup table from sRGB to linear;
   - a 4096-entry lookup table from linear back to sRGB;
   - the linear RGB of each palette colour and of the grout.

2. Give each cell an exact footprint, meaning the cell plus half of each neighbouring joint, with no outer joint at the border:
   - fw[col] = colW[col] + g/2·(col>0) + g/2·(col<cols−1)
   - fh[row] = rowH[row] + g/2·(row>0) + g/2·(row<rows−1)
   The footprints then add up to exactly finishedW × finishedH.

3. Compute the stone area and colour sum per cell:
   - FULL cells: covered = colW·rowH, using the c1 colour.
   - All other cells: loop over cellPieces(layout, data, row, col) and add area(poly)·lin(colour).
   Do not cache by line signature; computing the areas directly is cheap (73 ms for 667k cells).

4. Compute the mix: rest = max(0, A − covered), where A = fw·fh. Then mix = (Σ + rest·lin(grout)) / max(A, covered). The max() guards against FREE contours larger than the cell. Convert back to sRGB with the lookup table.

5. Pass the grout colour everywhere the overview is built:
   - In Viewer.tsx, pass props.groutHex and add it to the useMemo dependencies (around line 53). Otherwise changing the grout colour will not update the overview.
   - In renderFull, pass opt.groutHex ?? '#BDB8AE'.
   - StepPdf and useProject already pass groutHex to renderFull and need no change.

6. Add vitest cases in tests/:
   - joint 0 with only FULL cells: the overview pixel equals the palette hex exactly;
   - tile 5 mm, joint 1 mm: the overview pixel equals the hand-computed linear mix;
   - a LINE cell with a known 30/70 split: weighted correctly;
   - the function does not change data, and the stone counts stay the same.

7. Optional: add a small README note that the zoomed-out view and the PDF overview show the optical mix including grout.

Keep out of this change, as a separate finding: drawing progress and focus dimming in the overview branch (render.ts:165-168).

findings.title: Laying mode has no row/column orientation and no bulk marking; progress is only per tap or whole section

In Verlegemodus, dragging pans instead of marking, so a 40×50 cm portrait (5,969 stones) needs thousands of taps unless a whole 30×30 cm section is marked at once. 'Meine Projekte' does not show laying progress.

findings.title: Viewer redraws every visible stone on every pointer move; panning is 10 fps or worse on tablet-class CPUs
findings.problem: renderMosaic is immediate-mode. For each visible cell it sets fillStyle and calls fillRect. When pitch is 9 px or more it also draws the glaze image per cell, and for split cells it adds save, clip, drawImage, restore and stroke (render.ts:176 to 247). Viewer.draw runs this on every pointermove and wheel event (Viewer.tsx:55 to 78, 196 to 207). It also calls getComputedStyle on every frame (Viewer.tsx:75). Nothing is cached between frames, so the cost is set by the number of visible cells. That number is highest just above the overview threshold (pitch 3 px or more and cellCount ≤ 400k, render.ts:165).
findings.evidence: Tablet emulation (1280x800 at DPR 2, CDP CPU throttling 4x), 200x100 cm at 5 mm (55,778 positions), preview step, 20 pan moves per zoom level (browser-big.cjs with TABLET=1 THROTTLE=4, browser/t55k/result.json). rAF callback time: zoom step 4 median 80.9 ms, p95 122 ms; step 6 91.8 / 156 ms; step 16 99.7 / 164 ms; step 18 101 / 254 ms. 20 of 20 frames were long tasks at these levels. Desktop without throttling: 55k step 2 median 16 ms, p95 33.5 ms; 5M step 14 median 23.2 ms, p95 36.9 ms (browser/b55k, browser/b5m). CPU profile while panning (browser-prof-pan.cjs, browser/profpan/pan-4 and pan-16.cpuprofile): at the face-overview zoom fillRect is 20.6 % of all samples; at the nose zoom drawImage (glaze) is 16.1 % and fillRect 10.7 %. Script time (Sr = renderMosaic) is only 2 to 4 %, so the cost is the per-cell canvas calls. Screenshots: browser/profpan-montage.png. All paths are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/performance-scale/.
findings.proposal: Add a tile cache. Quantize the zoom into power-of-two buckets, render 256x256 device-pixel tiles into OffscreenCanvas or ImageBitmap, ideally in a render worker using canvas.transferControlToOffscreen. Keep an LRU of about 64 tiles. Each frame then only draws the roughly 20 to 40 tiles that intersect the view, scaled between buckets, and switches to exact tiles once interaction settles. An edit or progress change invalidates only the tile containing that cell. Draw the selection, sections and progress ticks as a light overlay layer. For pitch 3 to 8 px, fill tiles through ImageData (cell color into a Uint32Array) instead of one fillRect per cell. Apply the glaze once per tile with createPattern aligned to the grid, instead of one drawImage per stone. Read --viewer-bg once, not every frame.
corrected:
Phase 1 (M effort, recommended):

1. Add a back buffer in Viewer.tsx. Use an OffscreenCanvas, or a hidden canvas, sized to the viewport plus a margin of about 25 % on each side, in device pixels. Render it with the existing renderMosaic at the current scale, without the highlight and section overlays. Store the view (scale, ox, oy) it was rendered for.

2. Pan: each frame, copy the buffer onto the visible canvas with one drawImage at the pan offset. When the view nears the edge of the margin, shift the buffer contents with drawImage onto itself. Then call renderMosaic only for the newly exposed strips. Use a View whose width and height cover just the strip, translated with ctx.translate and clipped to the strip rect. visibleRange then limits the work to those cells.

3. Wheel and pinch zoom: while the gesture runs, draw the buffer scaled. About 120-150 ms after the last wheel or pinch event, render the buffer again at the exact scale.

4. Invalidation: the cache key is all the props in the existing draw-effect dependency list (Viewer.tsx:142-144): layout, version, palette, realistic, showCodes, progressMode, focusColor, groutHex, surface, plus DPR.
   - Any change to these re-renders the whole buffer once.
   - For a single-stone colour edit or a progress tap, re-render only that cell's rect, with clip and the restricted view. This needs the Viewer to receive the changed row and col from useProject.

5. Overlays: draw the highlight and the section borders and labels after the blit, every frame. They are a few dozen calls. Selecting a stone or a section then never invalidates the buffer.

6. Read --viewer-bg once, on mount and when the theme or data-theme changes, not in every frame.

7. Keep the glaze per cell inside the cached render. Do NOT replace it with one createPattern: edge columns and rows have different sizes (layout.ts:71-104), and cut or freeform pieces are polygons.

8. Add an e2e guard for requirement 18:
   - After a pan and a single-stone edit, compare getImageData of the cached viewer with a fresh uncached renderMosaic of the same view. The difference must be within an anti-aliasing tolerance.
   - Re-run pan-verify.cjs. Target: the rAF callback stays under 4 ms during pan at 4x throttle on the tablet profile.

Phase 2 (optional, L effort, only if Phase 1 is not enough on real Android devices):
- Use 256x256 device-pixel tiles in power-of-two scale buckets, with an LRU of about 64 tiles.
- Consider a render worker only if the mosaic data can be shared read-only and stays in sync with edits and progress.

Effort M, impact 3 (4 on tablets and phones). Keep src/core/render.ts output unchanged, because renderFull feeds the PDF preview and thumbnails. Implement the caching only in src/ui/project/Viewer.tsx.

1) Split rendering into a cached base layer and a cheap overlay.
   - Add an option to renderMosaic (or a thin wrapper) that skips the sections and highlight passes (render.ts:251-301). This keeps the base free of overlays.
   - Keep one base canvas of 1.5x to 2x the viewport size in device pixels. Use an OffscreenCanvas, or a detached canvas on older WebViews.
   - Render the base with the same renderMosaic call, using a View shifted by the margin.
   - Cache key: layout identity, data identity, version, progressVersion, palette identity, realistic, surface, showCodes, progressMode, focusColor, groutHex, background colour, dpr, view.scale.
   - Read --viewer-bg once (on mount and on theme or matchMedia change), not per frame.

2) Panning.
   - Snap view.ox and view.oy to multiples of 1/dpr. Then each frame is a single drawImage(base, integer device-pixel offset), plus a redraw of the section rectangles and the selection outline (the existing code at render.ts:251-301 moved into a drawOverlay function).
   - With integer offsets the blit is pixel-identical to a fresh render, so no visual approximation is introduced.
   - When the viewport leaves the cached margin, re-render the base around the new centre. This happens once every several hundred px of drag, not every frame. Optionally render only the newly exposed strips by clipping renderMosaic to them.

3) Wheel and pinch zoom.
   - For in-between frames, draw the cached base with a scale transform (temporarily blurry is acceptable).
   - Schedule an exact re-render 120-150 ms after the last zoom event.
   - Never leave a scaled frame as the final, settled image.

4) Invalidation (the correctness-critical part).
   - Any change of a key field throws away the whole base.
   - For single-stone edits and progress taps, re-render only the affected cell rectangle (cell bbox expanded by joint/2, from layout.colX/colW/rowY/rowH). Do this with ctx.save(); ctx.rect(...); ctx.clip(); renderMosaic(...); ctx.restore() on the base. That path still uses the exact same renderMosaic code.
   - Falling back to a full base re-render is always allowed.

5) Do NOT implement the following:
   - Grid-aligned createPattern glaze. It is wrong for cut edge columns and rows and for SUB/FREE polygons.
   - ImageData pixel fills inside renderMosaic. They snap joints and change PDF previews.
   - A separate render worker. It duplicates MosaicData and adds sync complexity.
   Revisit these only if on-device profiling still shows long frames after steps 1-4.

6) Tests.
   - Vitest or Playwright pixel test: a base blitted at an integer device-pixel offset equals a fresh renderMosaic of the shifted view (max channel diff <= 1).
   - e2e: edit a stone's colour and tap a stone in laying mode, then read the canvas pixel at that stone and assert it changed immediately. This proves there are no stale tiles.
   - Re-run browser-big.cjs with TABLET=1 THROTTLE=4. Target: pan frame median < 8 ms at wheel steps 4-18 (currently 80-101 ms).
   - Also report one measurement on a real Android device through the Capacitor APK, since all current numbers come from SwiftShader software rendering.

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
